- Purple (p) -> White (W)
- Yellow (W) -> Yellow (Y) (reverted!)
- Green (N) stayed green
So the pattern is:
- Each click toggles two shapes
- Click (14,44): toggles green and blue
- Click (38,17): toggles yellow and green
- Click (47,38): toggles purple/blue and yellow
This is like a toggle puzzle! Each red block toggles a pair of shapes. The goal is to get all three shapes to white.
Current state:
- Green (N)
- Yellow (Y)
- White (W) (was blue/purple)
I need to toggle green and yellow to white without changing the white shape.
Let me think about this:
- Click (14,44): toggles green and blue
- Click (38,17): toggles yellow and green
- Click (47,38): toggles blue and yellow
If I click (14,44) again, it will toggle green and blue:
- Green (N) -> White (W)
- Blue (W) -> Purple (p)
Then if I click (38,17), it will toggle yellow and green:
- Yellow (Y) -> White (W)
- Green (W) -> Green (N)
That doesn't work because it toggles green back.
Let me think more carefully. The shapes are:
1. Green (N) at top right
2. Yellow (Y) at middle left
3. Blue/Purple/White at bottom right
The toggles are:
- (14,44): toggles shape 1 and shape 3
- (38,17): toggles shape 2 and shape 1
- (47,38): toggles shape 3 and shape 2
Current state: N, Y, W
Goal: W, W, W
To get from N to W, I need to toggle shape 1.
To get from Y to W, I need to toggle shape 2.
To keep shape 3 as W, I need to toggle it an even number of times (0 or 2).
If I click (14,44) and (38,17):
- Shape 1: toggled twice (N -> W -> N) - no good
- Shape 2: toggled once (Y -> W) - good
- Shape 3: toggled once (W -> p) - no good
If I click (14,44), (38,17), and (47,38):
- Shape 1: toggled twice (N -> W -> N) - no good
- Shape 2: toggled twice (Y -> W -> Y) - no good
- Shape 3: toggled twice (W -> p -> W) - good
Hmm, this doesn't work either.
Wait, maybe the toggles are not exactly as I described. Let me re-examine:
Initial state: N, Y, b
After (14,44): W, Y, p
After (38,17): N, W, p
After (47,38): N, Y, W
So:
- (14,44): N->W, b->p
- (38,17): W->N, Y->W
- (47,38): p->W, W->Y
It seems like each click cycles the colors, not just toggles. Let me think about this as a state machine.
Actually, looking more carefully:
- Shape 1 (green): N -> W -> N -> ...
- Shape 2 (yellow): Y -> W -> Y -> ...
- Shape 3 (blue): b -> p -> W -> ...
So shape 1 and shape 2 toggle between two states, while shape 3 cycles through three states.
Current state: N, Y, W
To get W, W, W:
- Shape 1: N -> W (need 1 toggle)
- Shape 2: Y -> W (need 1 toggle)
- Shape 3: W -> ... (already W, need 0 toggles or 3 toggles)
If I click (14,44):
- Shape 1: N -> W (good)
- Shape 3: W -> b (bad)
If I then click (38,17):
- Shape 1: W -> N (bad)
- Shape 2: Y -> W (good)
If I then click (47,38):
- Shape 3: b -> p (still bad)
- Shape 2: W -> Y (bad)
This is getting complicated. Let me just try clicking (14,44) and see what happens.
